entries.title: Psalms 83:1
segments: A prayer in view of a formidable combination of the enemies of God's people to destroy them.  Some refer it to the combination of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, and others against Jehoshaphat, which is recorded in

entries.title: Psalms 83:3
segments: Thy hidden ones; thy people, whom thou hidest in thy pavilion from the assaults of their enemies.
The wicked have often sought the destruction of the righteous, but their plans have been defeated, and the ruin which they thought to bring upon others came upon themselves.

entries.title: Psalms 83:6
segments: Hagarenes; a people driven from their own lands by the tribe of Simeon, in the days of Saul.

entries.title: Psalms 83:7
segments: Gebal; supposed to have been a part of Idumea.

entries.title: Psalms 83:8
segments:
Assur; Assyria. 
 
  Children of Lot; Moab and Ammon.

entries.title: Psalms 83:10
segments:
Endor; near to mount Tabor, in the north part of Canaan. 
 
However numerous or formidable the enemies of the church, or however extensive the combinations formed against her, in answer to her prayers they will be overcome, scattered, and destroyed.

entries.title: Psalms 83:13
segments: Like a wheel; whirling like stubble or chaff before the wind.

entries.title: Psalms 83:16
segments: With shame; that is, dishonor, that by this chastisement they may be brought to seek thy name.  But some, in view of the following words, supply in the last clause of this verse the word "men," as is done in

, and render thus: "Fill their faces with shame; that men may seek thy name, O Lord. 
 
The Lord will be known by the judgments which he executes, and the destruction of the wicked will be an eternal monument of his truth, his justice, and his power.
